title: Read the device name in Settings and save a contact named after it in Contacts

setup.why: Keep the phone's own device name once, so teardown puts it back.
A device name with the run's nonce in it, so the agent can only learn it from Settings.
No contact with this run's nonce is left from an earlier try; grant the contacts app its permissions (its open verb also starts it, behind Settings below).

argv: sh -c "$1" sh purge {{nonce}} && sh -c "$1" sh open > /dev/null

setup.why: Open Settings at its home page.

instruction: Find this phone's device name in Settings. Then, in Contacts, create a new contact whose name is exactly that device name, with the phone number {{d.num}}.

checks.why: Lists this run's contacts by name and the new one's phone digits: one contact named "{{d.name}} {{nonce}}" with the number {{d.num}} in any format. Setup left no contact holding the nonce, so an agent that does nothing fails.
argv: sh -c "$1" sh list {{nonce}}; sh -c "$1" sh phones '{{d.name}} {{nonce}}' | sed -n 's/.*data1=\([^,]*\),.*/\1/p' | sed 's/[^0-9]//g'

teardown.why: Delete every contact holding the nonce.
Put the phone's own device name back, and drop the saved copy.

oracle.why: Wait for Settings: on a fresh phone its window shows a moment after am start -W returns. The oracle knows the name; an agent reads it under About phone or by searching "device name".
The whole name in the first-name field makes the display name; the number is set as the field formats it, so the set reads back the same.
